sections.title: One verb, two kinds of weather
sections.content: Just like süt and fúj, esik ("falls") puts the subject after the verb: Esik az eső. ("It's raining", literally "the rain is falling") and Esik a hó. ("It's snowing"). The same verb esik covers both — Hungarian doesn't need two separate verbs for rain and snow, only a different subject.

items.spanish: Ma egész nap esik az eső.
Nem esik, csak felhős az ég.
items.english: It's not raining, it's just cloudy.

sections.content: esik also means "to fall" in general — Leesik a könyv az asztalról. ("The book falls off the table.") So if you see esik outside a weather context, think "fall" rather than "rain".
